name: Anduril
description: Anduril is privately held and has no ticker. Review its funding rounds and valuations, the investors, funds and SPVs that hold its shares, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: Anduril Industries is a privately held defense technology company. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price; the principal public reference points are the valuations at which the company has raised capital. Its most recent financing, a $5 billion Series H round announced on May 13, 2026, valued the company at $61 billion.

Founded in 2017 and based in Costa Mesa, California, Anduril builds autonomous systems, sensors and weapons, together with Lattice, the software that connects them. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions, frequently through special purpose vehicles, and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.
figs: Special purpose vehicles with SEC filings naming Anduril
table_note: Valuations are as reported at the time of each round.
round_notes: Anduril has said that its revenue doubled in 2025, to $2.2 billion. In October 2026, Bloomberg reported that the company was arranging the sale of $1.3 billion of shares held by employees and other insiders at $94.80 per share, a price that implied a valuation of $90 billion.

A round valuation reflects the terms of the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz led the Series H. Founders Fund led the Series G and co-led the Series F with Sands Capital; Valor Equity Partners led the Series E and Elad Gil the Series D. Other investors include 8VC, General Catalyst, Lux Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Fidelity and Baillie Gifford.
spv_sentence: Since 2020, 87 special purpose vehicles formed to invest in Anduril have filed with the SEC, 25 of them in 2026.
funds: Mutual funds and other SEC-registered funds managed by Fidelity, Capital Group, J.P. Morgan, Franklin Templeton and BlackRock, among others, reported Anduril holdings in filings for periods in 2026. Capital Group's Growth Fund of America valued its position at $145.8 million as of May 31, 2026.
sources: Sources: reports by TechCrunch (May 2026, June 2025 and August 2024), CNBC (May 2026), SiliconANGLE (December 2022) and Bloomberg (October 2026); and SEC Form D and Form N-PORT filings.
